reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let n be a positive integer and h a nonnegative integer. Write [k] = {0,…,k−1}, L = [h+1], Q = 2^(64(h+1)), R = 2^(74(h+1)), and P = {p ∈ ℕ : p is even and 4 ≤ p ≤ Q}. Fix arbitrary deterministic real weights β_i and vectors x_i ∈ ℝ^[n] for i ∈ L, with the Euclidean norm on ℝ^[n].

For i ∈ L set m_i = h−i+1, J_i = [m_i], and S_i = ∑_{j∈J_i} R^j. For p ∈ P define
a_{i,p} = 1 / (p^4 S_i^2 √(m_i log(2 Q S_i))),
where log is the natural logarithm. Define the slot set D_{i,p} = [p] × {(j,t) : j ∈ J_i, t ∈ [R^j]}, the coordinate set C_{i,p} = {k : D_{i,p} → [n]}, and the real Euclidean coefficient block E_{i,p} = ℝ^{C_{i,p}}. The block labels are B = L × P. Let Ω = ℝ^{⨆_{(i,p)∈B} C_{i,p}} with its Euclidean norm, and let μ be the centered identity-covariance Gaussian probability measure on Ω. For ξ ∈ Ω, let ξ_{i,p} ∈ E_{i,p} be its coordinate restriction to block (i,p), with no rescaling.

For u = (u_j)_{j∈J_i} with u_j ∈ ℝ^[n] and z ∈ E_{i,p}, define the contraction
g_{i,p}(u,z) = √n a_{i,p} ∑_{k∈C_{i,p}} z(k) ∏_{(ℓ,j,t)∈D_{i,p}} u_j(k(ℓ,j,t)).
Let φ(t) = exp(−1/t) for t > 0 and φ(t) = 0 for t ≤ 0. For r ∈ ℝ set
χ(r) = [φ(r−13/20) / (φ(r−13/20)+φ(7/10−r))] · [φ(1−r) / (φ(1−r)+φ(r−19/20))].
Define the tail at level i by y_{i,j} = x_{i+j} for j ∈ J_i and the multiplier c_i = ∏_{j∈J_i} χ(‖y_{i,j}‖/√n). Define H_i(ξ) = 0 if any y_{i,j} is zero. Otherwise let u^{(i)}_j = y_{i,j}/‖y_{i,j}‖ and set H_i(ξ) = c_i ∑_{p∈P} g_{i,p}(u^{(i)},ξ_{i,p}).

Set W(ξ) = ∑_{i∈L} β_i H_i(ξ) and V = n ∑_{i∈L} β_i^2 c_i^2 (∑_{p∈P} a_{i,p}^2). Then V ≥ 0, W is μ-almost-everywhere measurable, and its pushforward W♯μ is the centered real Gaussian law of variance V (the point mass at zero when V = 0). The function ξ ↦ exp(−W(ξ)) is Bochner integrable under μ, and ∫_Ω exp(−W(ξ)) dμ(ξ) = exp(V/2).
objects: The deterministic weight family β and Euclidean-vector family x; finite level, degree, slot, and coefficient-coordinate sets; the normalizers S_i and a_{i,p}; the glue function φ, cutoff χ, tails y_{i,j}, and multipliers c_i; the Euclidean block spaces E_{i,p}, the aggregate coefficient space Ω, and its standard Gaussian μ; the coefficient restriction ξ_{i,p}, contraction g_{i,p}, level field H_i, scalar W, and variance V.
domains: n is a positive integer and h a nonnegative integer. Levels are i ∈ [h+1]; degrees p are even integers in [4,2^(64(h+1))], including the upper bound. Tail indices are j ∈ [h−i+1]. Each x_i and u_j belongs to ℝ^[n] with Euclidean norm, and each β_i is real. For each block (i,p), the slots are [p] × ⨆_{j∈[h−i+1]} [(2^(74(h+1)))^j], its coordinates are all functions from these slots to [n], and its coefficient arrays are real Euclidean arrays over that coordinate set. Ω is the real Euclidean space over the disjoint union of these coordinate sets, with block labels retained.
quantifiers: For every positive integer n, every nonnegative integer h, every real family β indexed by [h+1], and every family x indexed by [h+1] of vectors in ℝ^[n], the three conclusions hold for the displayed constructions. The indexed sums and products include every element of their respective finite sets.
assumptions: There are no restrictions on β or x beyond their domains; in particular, no nonzero-tail, unit-norm, cutoff-support, or positive-variance assumption is imposed. The coefficient vector alone is sampled under the centered identity-covariance Gaussian μ. The definition of H_i treats a zero vector anywhere in its own tail by setting H_i to zero; this branch is not a premise of the theorem.
conclusion: W is μ-almost-everywhere measurable and its μ-pushforward is the centered real Gaussian with variance V = n ∑_{i∈L} β_i^2 c_i^2 (∑_{p∈P} a_{i,p}^2), which is nonnegative (so truncation to a nonnegative real is inert); when V = 0 the law is the point mass at 0. The real-valued exp(−W) is Bochner integrable under μ, and its integral equals exp(V/2).
scopes: The choices n, h, β, and x are fixed before taking the law or integral; only ξ is random. The tail for a given level i uses x_i through x_h and its cutoff c_i multiplies the entire sum over degrees at that level. Its zero-tail test is per level. Each contraction uses only the coefficient restriction to its own (i,p) block, without rescaling, and uses the jth normalized tail vector in every slot with tail label j. The law and moment concern the same scalar W and the same aggregate standard Gaussian μ.
constant_dependencies: Q = 2^(64(h+1)) and R = 2^(74(h+1)) depend only on h. For i ∈ L, m_i = h−i+1 and S_i = ∑_{j=0}^{h−i} R^j depend only on h and i. The amplitude a_{i,p} = [p^4 S_i^2 √(m_i log(2 Q S_i))]⁻¹ depends only on h,i,p, and the contraction has prefactor √n a_{i,p}. The cutoff uses the fixed thresholds 13/20, 7/10, 19/20, and 1, and c_i depends on n and the given tail vectors through their norm ratios ‖x_{i+j}‖/√n. V depends on n,h,β,x via the displayed deterministic sum and does not depend on ξ; the Laplace identity is at exponent −W and has factor 1/2 in V/2.
